schematicCompat.title: Schematic Compatibility Tool
schematicCompat.description: Convert schematics between Minecraft versions and mod loaders

game.title: Game
game.comingSoonNotice: Hytale support is on the roadmap.

setup.worldUnresolved: {count} block ids are still unnamed — they were assigned by a different world.
setup.worldCaveat: Pre-1.13 files store mod blocks as plain numbers, and only the world they were built in knows what those numbers mean. It must be that same world: another save assigns the same numbers to different blocks.
setup.worldNeeded: {count} block types in this file are just numbers with no name — without the world's level.dat they cannot get a texture.

diff.emptyPrompt: Scan both environments, load a schematic, then press Analyze.
diff.bulkRulesDesc: Apply a rule to all unresolved blocks from each namespace at once.

guide.title: How to use
guide.step1: Pick the source environment folder — the Minecraft instance the schematic was built in.
guide.step2: Pick the target environment folder — the instance you want to load the schematic in.
guide.step3: Pick the schematic file (.schem, .litematic, .nbt, or .mca region).
guide.step4: Press Analyze to see which blocks are incompatible.
guide.step5: Set replacements in the Compatibility panel, then Export.

manualEnv.title: Which Minecraft version is this?
manualEnv.body: This folder has no launcher metadata we recognise. Tell us its version and mod loader and we'll scan it anyway — any mods found are still included.
manualEnv.jarsFound: {count, plural, =0 {No mod JARs found} one {# mod JAR found} other {# mod JARs found}}

error.instanceEmpty: That folder has no launcher metadata and no mods. Pick a game instance folder, or switch this environment to Vanilla.
error.exportTooLarge: This schematic is too large for the selected format. Export a smaller region, or choose .schem / .litematic.
error.levelDatUnreadable: That file could not be read as a level.dat.
error.levelDatNoRegistry: This level.dat has no Forge block registry, so there are no mod ids to resolve — it is either a vanilla world or from a version that stores them elsewhere.
